sections.content:
Population change in Maldon in 2032

The population in Maldon is projected to increase from 67,568 people in 2022 to 73,903 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net internal migration, which will increase the population by 9,055 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Maldon
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Maldon, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 2,687, with 5,690 births and 8,377 deaths in Maldon between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in Maldon by 4.0%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 9,055, with 44,558 people moving to the area and 35,504 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Maldon by 13.4%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 314, with 532 people moving to the area and 846 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Maldon by 0.5%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 303, with 1,425 people moving to the area and 1,122 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Maldon by 0.4%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Maldon in 2032

The median age in Maldon is projected to remain the same at 48 years between 2022 and 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 27% of the population in Maldon are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 24% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in Maldon between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Maldon is projected to stay the same, at around 58%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 402 to 427 over the same time period.

This is above average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Maldon?

In 2032, 19% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, around the same as in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Maldon between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 5% to 4%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will stay around the same, at 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
